application.source: classification mapping required by the facts audit brief
application.note: In-service EVs (readme; paper Note S1). The vehicle type is not disclosed.

chemistry.source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ensm.2026.105638 (read in arXiv 2608.10825), Supplementary Note 1 ('14 series-connected ternary cells') and Discussion ('ternary chemistries')

units_released.source: release readme ('real-world data from 99 in-service EVs') and https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ensm.2026.105638 (read in arXiv 2608.10825), p. 3 and Supplementary Note 1
units_released.note: Counted as stated (maintainer, 2026-11-20). Vehicle identifiers are not released, and snapshots cannot be linked to vehicles reliably (scripts/checks/li2026_evfault_link.py, reports/candidates/li2026_evfault/LINKING.md), so the files cannot rebuild the 99. Observation time is counted as system-hours from the snapshots.

cells_liion.source: release readme ('99 in-service EVs') and https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ensm.2026.105638 (read in arXiv 2608.10825), Supplementary Note 1 (each pack 14 series-connected cells)
cells_liion.note: Follows the 99 stated vehicles: 99 x 14. No parallel count is stated (ledger C1). Not measurable from the files.

cells_leadacid.note: No lead-acid cell count applies or is exposed in this release.

cell_channels_measured.source: scripts/facts/li2026_evfault.py: V 1 to V 14 in every snapshot
cell_channels_measured.note: 14 channels per snapshot. Which vehicle a snapshot comes from is not released.

energy_mwh.note: No rating, capacity or current is released.

obs_hours.source: 3,407 snapshots x 50 samples x 10 s (0.1 Hz, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ensm.2026.105638 (read in arXiv 2608.10825), p. 3) / 3600
obs_hours.note: System-hours from the windows, counted (maintainer, 2026-11-20): snapshot time only, assuming snapshots do not overlap (each is aligned to the end of a different charge, paper p. 6). Not the vehicles' service time.

fault_onset_timestamp.source: fielddata.loaders.li2026_evfault: labels per snapshot and cell, no time; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ensm.2026.105638 (read in arXiv 2608.10825), Note S1 (terminal thermal-runaway stage excluded)

sentinels_documented.source: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23980122; public data record and released documentation state no sentinel convention

charge_end_sample.note: Median over snapshots of the sample at which the 14-cell median voltage peaks (inference for the end of charging; interquartile range 24 to 24).

fault_batteries_stated.source: scripts/checks/li2026_evfault_fig1d.py -> reports/candidates/li2026_evfault/fig1d_summary.txt (read from the grid of the paper's Fig. 1D)
fault_batteries_stated.note: 87 of the 99 EVs carry at least one fault label; 12 are labelled fault-free only. Counted from the figure, not printed in the paper.

fault_label_cell_snapshots.note: Cell-snapshots with a non-zero code: EI 1,659, ASD 426, ACD 503, ISC 308. 2,236 snapshots have at least one labelled cell. Cell 14 carries 1,434 of them.

faults_stated.source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ensm.2026.105638 (read in arXiv 2608.10825), p. 3, Fig. 1D (EI 62, ASD 42, ACD 44, ISC 23 EVs); ACD's 44 EVs also on p. 8
faults_stated.note: Vehicle-level faults, once per vehicle and fault type (maintainer, 2026-11-24, ledger V1). The grid reading in scripts/checks/li2026_evfault_fig1d.py reproduces the printed counts.

snapshot_fault_labels.note: Snapshots with at least one labelled cell. Not the fault count (maintainer, 2026-11-24, ledger V1): Table 3 uses the paper's vehicle-level faults (faults_stated). Snapshots cannot be linked to vehicles, so each labelled snapshot is standalone. This overstates the number of faulty cells, since one faulty cell appears in many snapshots (paper Fig. 3F: 32 snapshots of one EV). Counted per labelled cell-snapshot it would be 2,896.

snapshots.source: scripts/facts/li2026_evfault.py: Data/0.csv to Data/3406.csv, none missing
snapshots.note: The readme says 3,408 labelled segments. The paper's 47,968 labelled samples compare with 3,407 x 14 = 47,698 cell-snapshots (digits transposed, probably).
